syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Types of solutions

concepts.learning_objective: Classify solutions by the physical states of solute and solvent with examples.
Identify the solvent of a solution and relate it to the physical state of the solution.

topics.title: Expressing concentration of solutions

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate mole fraction and mass percentage of components of a solution.
Calculate molarity and molality and explain their dependence on temperature.

topics.title: Solubility of solids and gases in liquids

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the solubility of solids in liquids using the like-dissolves-like principle.
Apply Henry's law and the effect of temperature to the solubility of gases in liquids.

topics.title: Vapour pressure of liquid solutions

concepts.learning_objective: Apply Raoult's law to find the vapour pressure and vapour composition of a mixture of volatile liquids.
Relate Raoult's law to Henry's law as a special case.
Explain why a non-volatile solute lowers the vapour pressure of a solvent.

topics.title: Ideal and non-ideal solutions

concepts.learning_objective: State the characteristics of ideal solutions.
Explain positive and negative deviations from Raoult's law in terms of intermolecular forces.
Distinguish minimum and maximum boiling azeotropes and relate them to deviations.

topics.title: Colligative properties and determination of molar mass

concepts.learning_objective: Define colligative properties and calculate the relative lowering of vapour pressure.
Calculate elevation of boiling point and depression of freezing point.
Use osmotic pressure to find molar mass and explain reverse osmosis.

topics.title: Abnormal molar masses

concepts.learning_objective: Use the van't Hoff factor to modify colligative property calculations.
Relate association and dissociation of solutes to abnormal molar masses and degree of dissociation.

topics.title: Electrochemical cells and galvanic cells

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish a galvanic cell from an electrolytic cell using the Daniell cell under an external opposing potential.
Represent a galvanic cell by the standard notation and relate electron flow, anode, cathode and emf.

topics.title: Measurement of electrode potential and the electrochemical series

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the standard hydrogen electrode is used to measure standard electrode potentials.
Use standard electrode potentials to compare oxidising and reducing power and predict feasibility of reactions.

topics.title: Nernst equation

concepts.learning_objective: Write the Nernst equation for an electrode and for a cell, with the correct number of electrons and concentration terms.
Calculate electrode and cell potentials at non-standard concentrations at 298 K.

topics.title: Equilibrium constant and Gibbs energy from cell potential

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the standard Gibbs energy of a cell reaction to its standard cell potential using ΔrG° = –nFE°cell.
Calculate the equilibrium constant of a cell reaction from its standard cell potential.

topics.title: Conductance of electrolytic solutions and its measurement

concepts.learning_objective: Define resistance, resistivity, conductance and conductivity and state their SI units and the factors affecting them.
Determine the cell constant and conductivity of a solution using a conductivity cell and AC Wheatstone bridge.
Calculate molar conductivity from conductivity and concentration with correct units.

topics.title: Variation of conductivity with concentration and Kohlrausch's law

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why conductivity decreases and molar conductivity increases on dilution for strong and weak electrolytes.
Apply Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions to find limiting molar conductivities.
Calculate the degree of dissociation and dissociation constant of a weak electrolyte from conductivity data.

topics.title: Electrolytic cells and electrolysis

concepts.learning_objective: Apply Faraday's laws of electrolysis to relate charge passed to the amount of substance deposited or liberated.
Predict the products of electrolysis using electrode potentials, the nature of electrodes and overpotential.

topics.title: Batteries, fuel cells and corrosion

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the construction and electrode reactions of the dry cell, mercury cell, lead storage battery and nickel-cadmium cell.
Explain the working of the hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell and its advantages.
Explain rusting of iron as an electrochemical process and evaluate methods of preventing corrosion.

topics.title: Rate of a chemical reaction

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish average rate from instantaneous rate and obtain each from concentration-time data.
Express the rate of a reaction in terms of any reactant or product using stoichiometric coefficients.

topics.title: Dependence of rate on concentration: rate expression and rate constant

concepts.learning_objective: Write and use a rate law, recognising that its exponents are found by experiment.
Interpret the rate constant as the rate when every reactant concentration is unity.

topics.title: Order of a reaction

concepts.learning_objective: Determine the order of a reaction from its rate law or from experimental rate data.
Relate the units of the rate constant to the order of the reaction.

topics.title: Molecularity and mechanism of a reaction

concepts.learning_objective: Define molecularity and distinguish it from order for elementary and complex reactions.
Deduce the rate law of a complex reaction from its slowest step and identify intermediates.

topics.title: Integrated rate equations for zero and first order reactions

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the integrated rate equation of a zero order reaction and explain why surface reactions can be zero order.
Use the integrated rate equation of a first order reaction to calculate k, time or concentration.

topics.title: Half-life and pseudo first order reactions

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate and compare the half-lives of zero and first order reactions.
Explain why some higher order reactions behave as pseudo first order reactions.

topics.title: Temperature dependence of rate and effect of catalyst

concepts.learning_objective: Use the Arrhenius equation to relate rate constant, temperature and activation energy.
Explain how a catalyst changes the rate of a reaction without changing its thermodynamics.

topics.title: Collision theory of chemical reactions

concepts.learning_objective: Relate collision frequency and activation energy to the rate of a bimolecular reaction.
Explain effective collisions in terms of threshold energy, orientation and the steric factor.

topics.title: Position and electronic configurations of the d-block elements

concepts.learning_objective: Identify transition elements using the IUPAC definition based on an incomplete d subshell in the atom or its ions.
Write and explain the (n-1)d ns configurations of d-block elements, including the exceptions Cr, Cu and Pd.

topics.title: Physical properties, atomic sizes and ionisation enthalpies

concepts.learning_objective: Relate high melting points and enthalpies of atomisation to the number of unpaired (n-1)d and ns electrons in metallic bonding.
Explain the trends in atomic and ionic radii and density across a transition series and between series.
Interpret irregularities in successive ionisation enthalpies of the 3d series using the stability of d5 and d10 configurations.

topics.title: Oxidation states and electrode potentials

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the variety of oxidation states of transition metals and their trends along a series and down a group.
Use E values of M2+/M and M3+/M2+ couples to judge reducing and oxidising behaviour of transition metal ions.
Explain why oxygen and fluorine stabilise the highest oxidation states of transition metals.

topics.title: Magnetic properties, colour, complexes, catalysis, interstitial compounds and alloys

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of a transition metal ion from its number of unpaired electrons.
Explain the colour of transition metal ions in terms of d-d transitions and identify colourless ions.
Describe the catalytic behaviour, interstitial compounds and alloys of transition metals and the reasons for them.

topics.title: Some important compounds: oxides, potassium dichromate and potassium permanganate

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the oxidation state of a transition metal in its oxide to the ionic, acidic or basic character of the oxide.
Describe the preparation, structure and oxidising reactions of potassium dichromate, including redox stoichiometry.
Describe the preparation, magnetic behaviour and oxidising reactions of potassium permanganate in different media.

topics.title: The lanthanoids

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the oxidation states and magnetic behaviour of lanthanoids to the stability of 4f0, 4f7 and 4f14 configurations.
Explain the cause of lanthanoid contraction and its consequences for the third transition series.
Recall the general properties, reactions and uses of lanthanoids such as mischmetall.

topics.title: The actinoids and applications of d- and f-block elements

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the electronic configurations, oxidation states and radioactivity of the actinoids.
Compare actinoids with lanthanoids in configuration, contraction, oxidation states and reactivity.
Recall industrial applications of d- and f-block elements and their compounds, especially as catalysts.

topics.title: Werner's theory of coordination compounds

concepts.learning_objective: State the postulates of Werner's theory, including primary and secondary valences and coordination polyhedra.
Deduce the formulation of a complex from the moles of AgCl it precipitates and its conductivity.
Distinguish a double salt from a complex by their behaviour in aqueous solution.

topics.title: Important terms: ligands, coordination number and coordination sphere

concepts.learning_objective: Classify ligands as unidentate, didentate, polydentate, chelating or ambidentate.
Determine the coordination number of the central atom/ion from the donor atoms bonded to it.
Identify the coordination sphere, counter ions, oxidation number and homoleptic or heteroleptic nature of a complex.

topics.title: Nomenclature of coordination compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Write formulas of mononuclear coordination entities using IUPAC rules.
Write IUPAC names of mononuclear coordination compounds, including complex anions.

topics.title: Isomerism in coordination compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Explain cis-trans and fac-mer isomerism and predict when it is possible.
Identify chiral coordination entities that show optical isomerism.
Distinguish linkage, coordination, ionisation and solvate isomerism with examples.

topics.title: Valence bond theory and magnetic properties

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the hybridisation of the central ion to the geometry of a complex using valence bond theory.
Use magnetic data and inner or outer orbital hybridisation to explain unpaired electrons and geometry.
State the limitations of valence bond theory.

topics.title: Crystal field theory and colour in coordination compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the splitting of d orbitals in octahedral and tetrahedral crystal fields.
Use the spectrochemical series and the relation between crystal field splitting and pairing energy to predict high or low spin.
Explain the colour of complexes as d-d transitions and relate the wavelength absorbed to the splitting energy.

topics.title: Metal carbonyls and applications of coordination compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the structures of homoleptic carbonyls and the synergic sigma and pi bonding in them.
Explain uses of complexes in analysis, metallurgy, industry, electroplating and photography.
Identify biologically important complexes and the use of chelate therapy in medicine.
